summary: RFC 8110 describes Opportunistic Wireless Encryption, which lets clients without credentials connect to a network with encrypted traffic. This informational document transfers maintenance and further development of the protocol to the IEEE 802.11 Working Group, and updates RFC 8110 to say so.

plainLanguage.summary: Opportunistic Wireless Encryption provides encrypted wireless traffic without authentication. This RFC says future maintenance and development will take place in the IEEE 802.11 Working Group.

subtitle: Transfers future OWE maintenance and development to the IEEE 802.11 Working Group.

tldr.problem: The IEEE 802.11 Working Group requested responsibility for OWE maintenance and development so it remains in sync with IEEE protocols.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 9672 records concurrence that future OWE work will occur in the IEEE 802.11 Working Group and that the protocol will be duplicated there.
tldr.outcome: The RFC updates RFC 8110 to note where future work will occur; it introduces no protocol or security changes.

today: RFC 9672 is an Informational document that updates RFC 8110. It records that future OWE work will occur in the IEEE 802.11 Working Group.

sections.title: Opportunistic Wireless Encryption
sections.content:
Opportunistic Wireless Encryption (OWE), defined in RFC 8110, is a mode of opportunistic security for IEEE 802.11. It encrypts the wireless medium without authentication.

The RFC says OWE, also known as Wi-Fi Enhanced Open, had been widely implemented and deployed since publication. The IEEE 802.11 Working Group requested the ability to maintain and develop it.
sections.plainLanguage: OWE encrypts wireless traffic without authenticating the client. This RFC records a change in which group will maintain the protocol.

sections.title: Transfer of Maintenance
sections.content:
RFC 9672 records concurrence that future work on OWE will occur in the IEEE 802.11 Working Group, to keep the protocol in sync with IEEE protocols.

The RFC says the IEEE working group will duplicate the OWE protocol so that its document alone is enough to implement, maintain and modify it under IEEE policies and procedures.
sections.plainLanguage: Future OWE work will take place in the IEEE 802.11 Working Group. The RFC says the group will maintain its own complete document.

sections.title: Security and IANA Considerations
sections.content: This document only notes where future work on the protocol described in RFC 8110 will occur. It introduces no new security considerations and has no IANA actions.
sections.plainLanguage: The RFC changes who will do future maintenance. It does not add security considerations or request IANA actions.
